factProposals.value: An ROI estimate takes user assumptions: a name, a currency, a horizon of 1 to 10 years, time savings (cases per year, minutes per case, automation rate, cost per hour), other yearly savings, one-off and yearly costs, and optional uncertainty for savings and costs. Any assumption may link to evidence: a STORY-002 analysis step or a STORY-007 document field.

Each estimate shows savings per item, annual savings, total costs, net benefit, ROI % and payback in months, each with its formula written out, for low, expected and high cases built from the stated uncertainty.
ROI scenarios are stored in PostgreSQL (roi_scenarios) with the assumptions exactly as submitted, the result, the warnings, status ok or needs_review, who calculated it and when.

Malformed assumptions are refused with every problem listed; figures too large to hold exactly are refused as a calculation error; zero total costs give 'ROI cannot be calculated' and yearly costs above savings give 'never pays back', never a misleading number.

Assumptions that look wrong are flagged and the estimate marked needs_review: automation above 90%, hours saved above one full-time person per item, cost per hour outside 10-250, ROI above 1000%, payback under a month, no uncertainty, and any disagreement with linked evidence (volume or duration more than 50% from the analysis, a cost more than 5% from the document, a different currency, or evidence that is missing or unconfirmed).

Only financial analysts and operations managers may calculate or view ROI estimates; documents used as evidence are read with the asking user's own access, so evidence they may not see counts as missing.
Every ROI calculation, refusal and calculation failure is in the audit log with the full assumptions as submitted, the headline figures and every warning.

ROI checks read saved STORY-002 process analyses (from their result store) and STORY-007 documents; the STORY-002 report now also records each activity's median duration as a number (medianDurationMs).

decisions.statement: Show core figures with a low/expected/high range from the user's stated uncertainty.
decisions.rationale: Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Detect incorrect assumptions with plausibility rules and by cross-checking linked evidence from process analyses and documents.

decisions.statement: Financial analysts and operations managers may calculate and view ROI.
decisions.rationale: Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Keep all money in whole minor units (pence, cents).
decisions.rationale: Floating-point totals drift (0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3); an ROI estimate must add up exactly.

decisions.statement: Warnings sit beside the numbers and never change them.
decisions.rationale: The estimate is the user's; the system's job is to show where it may be wrong, not to silently replace their judgement.

decisions.statement: Do not refuse workloads larger than one person's year.
decisions.rationale: A process is usually shared by a team; such volumes are flagged as a plausibility warning instead of refused.

limitations.statement: Only currencies with two decimal places, one currency per estimate, and no exchange rates.
No discounting: money in later years is valued the same as money now (no NPV).
Plausibility thresholds are fixed defaults (configurable in code, not by users), and the cost-per-hour range does not vary by currency or country.
Only assumptions explicitly linked to evidence are cross-checked; unlinked assumptions get plausibility checks only.
The sample process analysis covers 30 synthetic cases over 25 days, so the demo's sensible estimate is not linked to it; evidence checks against a real volume need a real analysis.
